## Hosted acceptance failure, not a demonstrated data defect

Current main `aa53d5f0e83f2df158d22aa5687b59e3493444fd` fails the [Node 22 job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/actions/runs/40926606362/job/123633690461): **883 tests, 882 passed, 1 failed**. Rechecked October 29 at 19:06 UTC: this remains the main revision, Node22 is failed and Node26 is still running. No claim of deployment or publication.

The failure is [test/idempotency.test.ts:587–610](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/blob/aa53d5f0e83f2df158d22aa5687b59e3493444fd/test/idempotency.test.ts#L587-L610), “PostgreSQL can serve each real idempotency sweep query with its partial age index”. At line602 it expects `idx_pm_idempotency_settled_at`, but the hosted plan is:

```
Delete on pm_idempotency_keys (cost=0.12..8.15 rows=0 width=0)
  -> Index Scan using idx_pm_idempotency_created_at ...
       Filter: ((status_code IS NOT NULL) AND (updated_at < ...))
```

This also does not demonstrate the age cutoff as an index condition. It does **not** establish wrong deletion semantics, data loss, or a production performance regression.

## Static context and source goal

The test extracts actual pending/settled sweep SQL, opens a transaction, disables sequential scans and asserts a specific index name and age Index Cond. It does not establish its own representative row distribution or ANALYZE statistics before EXPLAIN. Dependence on the existing test-table state/planner costs is a possible explanation, not an independently reproduced cause.

Both the legacy partial `created_at` index and the intended partial `updated_at` index exist in [schema.sql](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/blob/aa53d5f0e83f2df158d22aa5687b59e3493444fd/sql/schema.sql). The [real settled sweep](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/blob/aa53d5f0e83f2df158d22aa5687b59e3493444fd/src/idempotency.ts) filters on `updated_at`. A missing index is not demonstrated.

Canonical [pm-web-ccie](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/blob/aa53d5f0e83f2df158d22aa5687b59e3493444fd/.agents/pm/issues/pm-web-ccie.toon), particularly the October4 review-round4 receipts, requires meaningful real-query partial age-index proof and negative controls. Current CI does not satisfy that acceptance.

## Reproduction and acceptance

1. Inspect the linked immutable hosted log, or run the unchanged PostgreSQL-backed test/full Node22 suite in a disposable environment.
2. Determine whether table population/statistics, equivalent planner alternatives, retained legacy indexes, or SQL/index design causes this plan. Preserve the observed plan and database version/settings.
3. Make the acceptance fixture establish representative controlled rows/statistics and test the actual production predicates. Separate index capability/eligibility from cost-based planner selection where appropriate.
4. Keep a meaningful negative control that rejects missing/unusable age access paths; do not merely drop the assertion or accept any index scan. If alternate plans are admitted, justify their equivalent bounded work with query-plan/cost evidence.
5. Preserve retention/outcome semantics and schema parity. Run the focused case and full current-head Node22/26 gates with exact counts.

Scope: hosted failure plus static inspection; no local database, provider or concurrency reproduction. Three all-status issue/PR pages and the relevant canonical record were checked before filing. Existing #275 concerns unrelated history-version/lifecycle assertions and is not this failure.
